name: Cache Tags CDN Optimizer
description: Reshapes Drupal core cache tags for referenced entities into custom 'reference' tags and invalidates them only when configured fields change, so CDN/purge clears cached pages only when necessary.
project_description: The Cache Tags CDN Optimizer module optimizes Drupal's cache invalidation by rewriting standard entity cache tags for *referenced* entities into custom 'reference' tags (e.g. node:123 becomes node:reference:123), then invalidating those reference tags only when specific configured fields of the referenced entity actually change. This prevents unnecessary cache invalidation and CDN purges when a referenced entity is edited but nothing that appears on the referencing pages changed. It works entirely through Drupal core's cache-tag system: an onKernelResponse event subscriber rewrites the response's cache-tags header, and entity insert/update/delete hooks call Cache::invalidateTags(). It also optionally adds a per-path cache tag (useful for evicting cached 404s) and a bundle-level purge_all tag. The module talks to no external service itself; it shapes tags for whatever purge/CDN integration the site already runs. Configure it at Administration > Configuration > Services > Cache Tags CDN Optimizer, where you pick which fields per content type and vocabulary should trigger invalidation, toggle node/taxonomy replacement, set a blocklist, and optionally enable debug logging. Maintained by dseven GmbH.
